lines.trans: As you know, I debuted at thirteen—so I have never really done ordinary things properly.
I never had a normal school life, never went on a college retreat, and never drank alcohol properly either.
If you do not know alcohol, you do not know life.
Give this a sip—it will be a whole new world you have never tasted anywhere before.
I made my debut at thirteen! So this career is in its tenth year now—in idol years, that is turning sixty!
I debuted at thirteen, age thirteen! I was thirteen!
She keeps repeating the exact same story over and over—she has a drinking habit!
It appears her tipsy alter ego has arrived.
If only I had never gone to that amusement park at thirteen! What could a thirteen-year-old debuting possibly know?!
I am so sorry—I really want to go home now!

meanings.note: Used as noun + copula + -인데 (10년째인데).

examples.text: 내가 데뷔를 13살에 했어요. 그래서 이 생활이 지금 10년째인데 이게 아이돌 나이로 하면 환갑이라고!
examples.trans: I made my debut at thirteen! So this career is in its tenth year now—in idol years, that is turning sixty!
This point about in its tenth year, and is really important.

meanings.note: Used as native numeral + counter + -에 (13살에).

examples.text: 저는요 데뷔를 13살에 했잖아요. 보통 뭘 이렇게 제대로 해본 게 없어요.
examples.trans: As you know, I debuted at thirteen—so I have never really done ordinary things properly.

examples.text: 내가 데뷔를 13살에 했어요. 그래서 이 생활이 지금 10년째인데 이게 아이돌 나이로 하면 환갑이라고!
examples.trans: I made my debut at thirteen! So this career is in its tenth year now—in idol years, that is turning sixty!

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

가보다.gloss: to go and see; to visit

meanings.en: to go and check; to go see
meanings.note: Compound of 가다 ('to go') + 보다 ('to see/try').
Often used in past tense 가 봤다 for experiential meaning.

examples.trans: I'll have to go see for myself.
Have you ever been to Jeju Island?

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So how is it?
So I went.
Did you hear about this that person?
I was busy today because of that person.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 이제 준모도 나이를 먹을 만큼 먹었고 스스로 결정하게 해주시는 게 어떨까요.
examples.trans: Joon-mo is old enough now, so maybe it would be best to let him decide for himself.
Here the word for 'age' is key.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun (놀이공원).

examples.text: 놀이공원 측에서 연락 왔는데요, 야외 취침할 장소 포인트는 직접 보셨으면 하던데요.
examples.trans: The amusement park contacted us—they hoped you would inspect the outdoor sleeping spot in person.

examples.text: 13살에 놀이공원만 안 갔어도! 나 13살에 데뷔해서 뭘 아냐고!
examples.trans: If only I had never gone to that amusement park at thirteen! What could a thirteen-year-old debuting possibly know?!
Did you hear about this debut?
I was busy today because of debut.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 넌 무슨 소리를 하는 거니, 원래는 가수로 데뷔했고 어마어마한 히트곡 있잖아!
examples.trans: What on earth are you saying—he originally debuted as a singer and has massive hit songs!
This expression comes from 'debuted and'.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (마셔본).

examples.text: 학교생활도 제대로 해본 적도 없고, MT 가본 적도 없고, 술도 제대로 마셔본 적도 없고.
examples.trans: I never had a normal school life, never went on a college retreat, and never drank alcohol properly either.

examples.text: 마셔봐요, 이게 어디에서도 맛보지 못한 신세계일 거예요.
examples.trans: Give this a sip—it will be a whole new world you have never tasted anywhere before.

meanings.note: Used as verb + -지 (맛보지).

examples.text: 마셔봐요, 이게 어디에서도 맛보지 못한 신세계일 거예요.
examples.trans: Give this a sip—it will be a whole new world you have never tasted anywhere before.
Let us do that (taste) right away.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
I understand well (usually).
Today is a (usually) busy day.
Did you hear about this career, life?
I was busy today because of career, life.
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.

meanings.note: Used as noun + prospective copula (신세계일).

examples.text: 마셔봐요, 이게 어디에서도 맛보지 못한 신세계일 거예요.
examples.trans: Give this a sip—it will be a whole new world you have never tasted anywhere before.
This point about a whole new world is really important.

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.
Did you hear about this idol?
I was busy today because of idol.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Used as acronym noun (MT).

examples.text: 학교생활도 제대로 해본 적도 없고, MT 가본 적도 없고, 술도 제대로 마셔본 적도 없고.
examples.trans: I never had a normal school life, never went on a college retreat, and never drank alcohol properly either.
This point about membership training trip is really important.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그냥 어제를 내 인생에서 확 도려내버리고 싶다.
examples.trans: I just want to carve yesterday right out of my life.
Here the word for 'from my life' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.text: 그냥 내버려 둬, 쟤 완전 취했어.
examples.trans: Just leave him alone, he is completely wasted.
The topic of that guy/girl came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 ('have/haven't ever done')

examples.trans: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 그런 말은 처음 들어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.trans: I've heard something like that before.
I understand well (properly).
Today is a (properly) busy day.

meanings.note: Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 술만 먹었다 하면 끊어지는 너의 망할 주사, 진짜 고마워 준모야!
examples.trans: Your wretched drinking habit of blacking out every time you touch alcohol—thank you so much, Joon-mo!
Here the word for 'drinking habit' is key.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + -도 (학교생활도).

examples.text: 학교생활도 제대로 해본 적도 없고, MT 가본 적도 없고, 술도 제대로 마셔본 적도 없고.
examples.trans: I never had a normal school life, never went on a college retreat, and never drank alcohol properly either.
This point about school life too is really important.
I want to even try right now.
How about trying to even try together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as noun + quotative (환갑이라고!).

examples.text: 내가 데뷔를 13살에 했어요. 그래서 이 생활이 지금 10년째인데 이게 아이돌 나이로 하면 환갑이라고!
examples.trans: I made my debut at thirteen! So this career is in its tenth year now—in idol years, that is turning sixty!
This point about is a sixtieth birthday is really important.
